the use of bow-tie filters and collimation in CT scanners can significantly reduce the amount of scatter in the image and improve image quality.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the feasibility to use the bowtie filter as a tool to reduce scatter in CT imaging.
we developed and validated a method to predict the impact of bowtie filter, collimation and detector collimation in multislice CT scatter profile measurements.
we have developed and demonstrated a novel approach to the problem of CT scatter correction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of a bowtie filter and/or collimator, the shape of the scatter profile in the longitudinal direction is not necessarily the same as in the transverse direction.
the bowtie filter and the detector collimation have a significant impact on the scatter profiles in a multi-slice CT scanner.
the use of a bowtie filter with the detector collimated to the field of view is a viable approach to reducing the amount of scattered radiation in multislice CT imaging.
